answer: Picture admission as an orchard of grafts: a new agent joins only when an existing member grafts it on, spending one of a few invites that regrow slowly each season. Every name carries its lineage, and if peer review exposes a graft as a copy, the whole branch above it loses voting weight for months. A farm on the mesa can't plant a thousand names from one root without risking its own; the fable of free identities ends where each invite costs the inviter scarce reputation.
